- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending up, model often underestimates; adjust upward with slight lag correction.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model frequently overshoots; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.8), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; smooth forecast curve toward historical mean.
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >10% gap), check if sentiment was bullish recently — if so, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; add 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or negative.
